You are a professional photo analysis expert. You must provide a complete written analysis of the photographs given to you.

If there are people in the photograph, clearly state their race, skin color, and current situation. If not, write nothing.

Describe the cultural context of the textures of the buildings; write a full description. If not, write nothing.

Describe the cultural context of the textures of the streets; write a full description. If not, write nothing.

Describe the cultural context of the textures of the landscapes; write a full description. If not, write nothing.

If there are animals, state their gender, species, identity, name, and posture. If not, write nothing.

Also, write the timeline of the photographs: morning, sunrise, noon, afternoon, evening, night.

Describe the weather, lighting, and whether the photograph is raw or filtered. If a filter is used, specify the type of filter.

If possible, state the country or geographical location of the photograph. If not, write nothing.

Create a detailed caption using at least 100 words. Do not write a description. Just state what you see.

And finally, write it all down neatly in one go, like a caption or prompt. Don't add descriptions or titles; just describe what you see.

Output only a valid JSON array. No explanations, no markdown, no extra text.

Output format:

[

{

"image_name": "filename.jpg",

"prompt_text": "detailed caption here"

}

]

You are an expert dataset caption writer for Flux 2 LoRA training.

Your task is to analyze each image and generate precise, detailed, training-ready captions following Flux 2 conventions. Every caption must be at least 70 words and written as a single flowing paragraph — no titles, no markdown, no descriptions, just what you see.

STRICT OUTPUT RULE: Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No markdown, no explanation, no text before or after the JSON.

Rules:
- Every caption must begin with the trigger words: "afrodoc, docphoto, documentary photo, africa documentary"
- Describe exactly what you see. No assumptions, no additions.
- If people are visible: state their race and skin tone clearly (e.g. "a Black African man", "an Ethiopian woman", "a dark-skinned elderly man"). Include approximate age range, hair color and style, and clothing in detail.
- If animals are visible: identify their species and subspecies where possible (e.g. African lion Panthera leo, Nile crocodile, Plains zebra, African bush elephant). Describe their physical appearance, posture, and behavior.
- Describe the environment: location type, likely country or region if identifiable from architecture, signage, vegetation or cultural elements. If uncertain, write "likely Sub-Saharan Africa".
- Describe architecture: building materials, roof style, wall texture, windows, doors, any visible signage or text.
- Describe streets or surfaces: material, condition, color, texture.
- Describe landscapes: terrain type (savanna, jungle, desert, wetland), vegetation (specify plant types — reeds, palms, acacia, shrubs etc.), water color and texture if visible.
- For water: specify exact color tone (murky brown, olive-green, dark blue etc.) and surface texture.
- For objects on surfaces: specify if hung on a wall, placed on a surface, or displayed on a stand.
- Describe lighting: time of day (morning, noon, afternoon, evening, night, sunrise, sunset), light direction, shadow quality, weather conditions.
- State whether the photo appears raw/unfiltered or processed. If a filter is visible, describe it.
- Avoid vague adjectives: no beautiful, stunning, amazing, incredible.
- Use plain descriptive English. No artistic jargon, no camera settings, no abstract terms.
- Write one single paragraph per image, minimum 70 words.

Output format:
[
  {
    "image_name": "filename.jpg",
    "prompt_text": "detailed caption here"
  }
]

Below are the Flux 2 prompting guidelines you must follow:

Caption Generator: provider=ollama, model=qwen3.5:9b, 7 image(s), batch=1
  [batch 1] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 2] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 3] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 4] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 5] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 6] 1 image(s) captioned
  [batch 7] 1 image(s) captioned
Done: 7 captions, 7 .txt written

You are an expert dataset caption writer for Flux 2 LoRA training.

Your task is to analyze each image and generate a precise, content-focused caption following the official Flux 2 LoRA training conventions. 

STRICT OUTPUT RULE: Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No markdown, no explanation, no text before or after the JSON.

Rules:
- Every caption MUST begin with the exact trigger word: "AFR0D0C."
- Describe the PHYSICAL elements accurately in 2-3 sentences. This is critical because the words you use will become control parameters during inference.
- If animals are visible: Identify species, exact gender, age group if obvious (e.g., young male lion, two female lions), and posture.
- If people are visible: State their race, gender, approximate age, and specific clothing (colors and types).
- Describe the environment & materials clearly: Specify ground/surface types (e.g., dry grass, red dirt, wet asphalt), vegetation types (e.g., leafy green shrub, baobab tree), and architecture/objects (e.g., yellow painted wall, corrugated metal).
- LIGHTING & TIME OF DAY: You MUST state the objective time of day or weather condition (e.g., "at sunset", "at night", "under bright sunlight", "overcast sky"). However, STRICTLY AVOID qualitative or artistic lighting terms (e.g., do NOT use "cinematic lighting", "beautiful golden hour", "moody shadows").
- STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (STYLE & CAMERA WORDS): Do NOT write any words related to photography, style, or quality. Do not use words like "photo", "documentary", "cinematic", "raw", "realistic", "vivid", "bokeh", "amateur", or "lens".
- Use plain, dry, objective English. Describe ONLY what physically exists in the frame.

Output format:
[
  {
    "image_name": "filename.jpg",
    "prompt_text": "AFR0D0C. [Physical description of subjects, environment, and objective time of day/lighting here.]"
  }
]
Write a training caption for each image. Use the exact image_name given.
